Precision handling. A direct contribution to advanced technology. As a Cleanroom Logistics Operator in ASML's FOUP & Reticle department, you ensure that essential materials and tools arrive safely, cleanly and on time where they are needed. You handle specialised items such as FOUPs and reticles. FOUPs are containers that protect wafers from contamination and damage during storage and transport. Reticles are highly precise glass plates carrying the patterns used in the lithography process. These delicate materials require careful handling, and you help keep them protected and available for production. This is a largely hands-on role with a smaller administrative component. You work in a controlled cleanroom, wear protective clothing and follow strict hygiene and safety procedures. Working a five-shift schedule, including early, late and night shifts, you support the continuity of production together with your colleagues. Your responsibilities include: - Transporting materials, tools, FOUPs and reticles within the cleanroom and to production departments. - Handling delicate components carefully to prevent contamination or damage. - Checking materials for completeness and quality, and reporting discrepancies. - Packing and preparing components for assembly or testing. - Recording inventory movements and the issue and return of materials. - Following cleanroom procedures, work instructions and safety requirements. - Coordinating with production and logistics colleagues to keep materials available. - Supporting the smooth operation of machines and assembly processes. Together we work on DEME's vision of creating a sustainable future.  -  Offshore -  Operations -  Worldwide  - Being responsible for the engineering, preparation and execution of our projects; - developing method statements for our works before we go execute them offshore; - when on site, optimizing and implementing the method statements in practice; - communicating between site or vessel and the office; - keeping track of the installation process on the bridge on board one of our vessels; - monitoring the progress of the project, participate in coordinating activities in the field, optimize and fine-tune where necessary in support of the Works Manager or Superintendent; - taking care of ad hoc needs of the project and actively respond to questions from the project management; - ensuring planning, production reporting, budget control and cost monitoring.  - Bachelor's degree (BSc) in Electromechanics, Civil Engineering, or a related discipline; or Master's degree (MSc) in Offshore Engineering, Marine Engineering, or a related discipline; - willingness to work abroad on our vessels or projects and in the office; - fluent in verbal and written English; - minimum of 3 years of proven experience in the offshore industry is required; - excellent team player.  - An extensive mobility program for a healthy work-life balance; - a permanent training track which allows you to develop yourself personally and professionally; - a stimulating, innovative workplace with numerous growth opportunities; - a people-oriented environment with an interactive health program and a focus on employee wellbeing. ...
